reviewed_by: Gemini Pro blind reviewer, batch G3-NA-Q1-Harden (mat_g3_na_q1_5), 2026-08-18

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The sample packet thoroughly fulfills the MATATAG competency 'Compare numbers up to 10 000 using the symbols =, >, and <.' All items require students to determine the relational inequality or equality between two numbers. Direct symbolic comparison items such as 'Compare the numbers: 71 ___ 71. Which sign is correct: >, <, or =?' (seed 42) and contextual comparison problems like 'Ben has 171 marbles. Jose has 180 marbles. Which sign correctly compares the two amounts?' (seed 43) directly target comparing two numerical quantities using the target relational symbols.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The items comprehensively cover all comparison outcomes (greater than, less than, and equal to) and digit magnitude configurations up to 10 000. It tests equal values in both 2-digit and 4-digit scales ('Compare the numbers: 71 ___ 71. Which sign is correct: >, <, or =?' [seed 42], 'Compare the numbers: 5765 ___ 5765. Which sign is correct: >, <, or =?' [seed 502]), strict less-than comparisons ('Compare the numbers: 3837 ___ 6709. Which sign is correct: >, <, or =?' [seed 501]), and strict greater-than comparisons ('Jose has 173 storybooks. Liza has 150 storybooks. Which sign correctly compares the two amounts?' [seed 72]). It also addresses comparing numbers with unequal digit lengths ('Compare the numbers: 12 ___ 200. Which sign is correct: >, <, or =?' [seed 44]) and numbers with identical leading digits ('Compare the numbers: 219 ___ 210. Which sign is correct: >, <, or =?' [seed 46]).

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The reading load, contextual framing, and mathematical reasoning are well-calibrated for Grade 3 Quarter 1 learners. Word problems use concise, culturally resonant Philippine names and familiar objects without unnecessary linguistic clutter, as in 'Ben has 242 pencils. Liza has 90 pencils. Which sign correctly compares the two amounts?' (seed 45) and 'Jose has 113 seashells. Liza has 120 seashells. Which sign correctly compares the two amounts?' (seed 603). True/false verification items like '111 < 90. True or False?' (seed 50) provide succinct cognitive checks without extraneous cognitive load.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The packet employs a balanced mix of formats including standard multiple choice ('Compare the numbers: 217 ___ 30. Which sign is correct: >, <, or =?' [seed 602]), cloze completion ('Maria has 146 marbles. Ben has 146 marbles. Which sign correctly compares the two amounts?' [seed 601]), and true/false relational validation ('5497 = 5956. True or False?' [seed 500]). It balances pure symbolic prompts with real-world quantity comparisons ('Kuya Pat has 158 pencils. Maria has 60 pencils. Which sign correctly compares the two amounts? The answer is cannot be determined. True or False?' [seed 605]).

competency_alignment.rationale: All items remain strictly aligned with the scope of Grade 3 Quarter 1 number comparison. There is no inclusion of multi-step arithmetic, ordering sequences of multiple numbers, decimal numbers, or negative values. Questions strictly evaluate comparisons of positive integers up to 10 000 using relational symbols =, >, and <, such as 'Compare the numbers: 20 ___ 112. Which sign is correct: >, <, or =?' (seed 600) and 'Jose has 60 storybooks. Maria has 52 storybooks. Which sign correctly compares the two amounts?' (seed 604).

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The numerical scale adheres precisely to the 'up to 10 000' ceiling of the learning competency. The sample spans 2-digit numbers ('Compare the numbers: 71 ___ 71. Which sign is correct: >, <, or =?' [seed 42]), 3-digit numbers ('Jose has 173 storybooks. Liza has 150 storybooks. Which sign correctly compares the two amounts?' [seed 72]), and 4-digit numbers up to thousands place comparisons ('Compare the numbers: 3837 ___ 6709. Which sign is correct: >, <, or =?' [seed 501], '5497 = 5956. True or False?' [seed 500]). All tested values are well within the 10 000 limit.
